title: Inverse and constraint path expansion under total oplax conjugation
statement:
Let $\mathcal A_0,\mathcal A_1,\mathcal B_0,\mathcal B_1$ be abelian monoidal categories [def-sp-abelian, def-sfb-monoidal-category], small relative to a fixed containing universe. Assume their tensors are additive in each variable, all small colimits exist, and tensoring on either side preserves them [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Let $E_j:\mathcal A_j\to\mathcal B_j$ ($j=0,1$) be additive strong monoidal equivalences, and let $F_{\mathrm i}:\mathcal A_0\to\mathcal A_1$ and $F_{\mathrm s}:\mathcal B_0\to\mathcal B_1$ be additive strong monoidal functors preserving countable coproducts [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor]. Fix an arbitrary natural isomorphism $a:E_1F_{\mathrm i}\cong F_{\mathrm s}E_0$, not assumed monoidal. For each of these functors $G$ write $\gamma^G_{M,N}:G(M\otimes N)\cong GM\otimes GN$ for its inverse tensorator and $\epsilon^G:G\mathbf1\cong\mathbf1$ for its oplax unit. Use unbounded integer cochain complexes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], their signed direct-sum tensor total [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso], and the associator and unitors induced from the ordinary ones [lem-sfb-total-tensor-homotopy]. Extend functors and $a$ termwise. Write $T_G:G\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes Q)\cong\operatorname{Tot}(GP\otimes GQ)$ for the canonical preserved-coproduct comparison with summand maps $\gamma^G_{P^p,Q^q}$, and $j_G:G(\mathbf1[0])\cong\mathbf1[0]$ for $\epsilon^G$ in degree zero and the canonical zero-object comparisons elsewhere. Define
$$\widetilde\gamma_{M,N}=(a_M\otimes a_N)\,\gamma^{E_1}_{F_{\mathrm i}M,F_{\mathrm i}N}\,E_1(\gamma^{F_{\mathrm i}}_{M,N})\,a_{M\otimes N}^{-1}\,F_{\mathrm s}((\gamma^{E_0}_{M,N})^{-1}),$$
and define the chain isomorphism
$$A_{P,Q}=(a_P\otimes a_Q)\,T_{E_1}\,E_1(T_{F_{\mathrm i}})\,a_{\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes Q)}^{-1}\,F_{\mathrm s}(T_{E_0}^{-1}):F_{\mathrm s}\operatorname{Tot}(E_0P\otimes E_0Q)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Tot}(F_{\mathrm s}E_0P\otimes F_{\mathrm s}E_0Q).$$
Composition in these formulas is from right to left.
The inverse of this specified conjugation has the summand formula
$$ (A_{P,Q}^{-1})^n\iota'_{p,q}=F_{\mathrm s}(\iota_{p,q})\widetilde\gamma_{P^p,Q^q}^{-1}.$$
It is a chain map for the differential $d_P\otimes1+(-1)^p1\otimes d_Q$ and satisfies both inverse equations as chain maps. Put
$$\widetilde\epsilon=\epsilon^{E_1}E_1(\epsilon^{F_{\mathrm i}})a_{\mathbf1_{\mathcal A_0}}^{-1}F_{\mathrm s}((\epsilon^{E_0})^{-1}),\qquad J=j_{E_1}E_1(j_{F_{\mathrm i}})a_{\mathbf1_{\mathcal A_0}[0]}^{-1}F_{\mathrm s}(j_{E_0}^{-1}).$$
Then $J:F_{\mathrm s}(\mathbf1_{\mathcal B_0}[0])\to\mathbf1_{\mathcal B_1}[0]$ is $\widetilde\epsilon$ in degree zero and the unique maps between zero objects otherwise.

For complexes $P,Q,H$, take the two paths of the internal oplax associator diagram for $F_{\mathrm i}$ and transport the whole diagram by $E_0,E_1,a$ and their specified total comparisons. In degree $n$, restrict either transported path along the image under $F_{\mathrm s}$ of a nested triple-summand inclusion of degrees $(p,q,r)$ with $p+q+r=n$. Its restriction is precisely the corresponding ordinary oplax associator path, transported by the ordinary $E_0,E_1,a$ comparisons at $P^p,Q^q,H^r$, followed by the matching target triple-summand inclusion. This assertion is about each of the two specified paths, including their intermediate comparison maps. The corresponding assertion holds for each path of each transported unitor diagram: the only possibly nonzero summands have degrees $(0,n)$ on the left and $(n,0)$ on the right, and their restrictions are the ordinary transported unitor paths with $\widetilde\epsilon$; the other summands have zero maps. These restrictions determine the whole chain maps even for infinite degreewise sums. Thus equality of the corresponding ordinary transported constraint paths implies equality of these total constraint paths. This assertion imposes no flatness or boundedness and no monoidality hypothesis on $a$.
Explicitly, put $G=F_{\mathrm s}E_0$, $h_{M,N}=\gamma^{E_0}_{M,N}$, $g_{M,N}=\widetilde\gamma_{M,N}F_{\mathrm s}(h_{M,N})$, and $\widehat A_{P,Q}=A_{P,Q}F_{\mathrm s}(T_{E_0;P,Q})$. Write $e=\widetilde\epsilon F_{\mathrm s}(\epsilon^{E_0})$ and $\widehat J=JF_{\mathrm s}(j_{E_0})$. With $M=P^p,N=Q^q,L=H^r$, the two paths
$$(1\otimes\widehat A_{Q,H})\widehat A_{P,\operatorname{Tot}(Q\otimes H)}G(\alpha^{\mathrm{Ch}}),\qquad \alpha^{\mathrm{Ch}}(\widehat A_{P,Q}\otimes1)\widehat A_{\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes Q),H}$$
restrict along $G$ of the source triple inclusion to the target triple inclusion composed, respectively, with
$$(1\otimes g_{N,L})g_{M,N\otimes L}G(\alpha_{M,N,L}),\qquad \alpha_{GM,GN,GL}(g_{M,N}\otimes1)g_{M\otimes N,L}.$$
The two left-unit paths restrict to $G(\lambda_M)$ and $\lambda_{GM}(e\otimes1)g_{\mathbf1,M}$; the right-unit paths restrict to $G(\rho_M)$ and $\rho_{GM}(1\otimes e)g_{M,\mathbf1}$. Removing $F_{\mathrm s}(T_{E_0})$ and $F_{\mathrm s}(j_{E_0})$ gives the stated path restrictions for $A,J$ themselves. All these are identities of restrictions of specified maps, before any equality with the separate $F_{\mathrm s}$ tensor comparison is asserted.

source.place: Tag 0FPQ, lemma-symmetric-monoidal-cat-complexes, proof hints for the degree-zero unit and tensor constraints; agent extraction of inverse and constraint path transport through a functor square, original item Steps 3-4.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-termwise-strong-monoidal] to the four functors: each equivalence $E_j$ is a left adjoint of its quasi-inverse and so preserves all small colimits, in particular countable coproducts [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits]; the tensor-total cocones needed are also explicitly supplied by [lem-pd-total-oplax-conjugation-summands]; and the two other functors preserve them by hypothesis. Thus each $T_G,j_G$ is a natural chain isomorphism for the specified signed tensor. The termwise $a$ is a chain isomorphism: its degreewise chain equation is precisely its naturality for $d_P$. Consequently the displayed composite $A$ is a chain isomorphism. The summand lemma gives, with $v_{p,q}=F_{\mathrm s}(\iota_{p,q})$ and $w_{p,q}=\iota'_{p,q}$,
$$A^nv_{p,q}=w_{p,q}\widetilde\gamma_{P^p,Q^q}.$$
Here and below products mean composition from right to left.

source.place: Tag 0FPQ, lemma-symmetric-monoidal-cat-complexes, proof hints on the degree-zero unit and the induced constraints; agent calculation for the specified functor-square conjugation.

proof.text:
Each $\widetilde\gamma_{M,N}$ is invertible, being a composite of the specified isomorphisms. Multiply the preceding restriction equation on the left by $(A^n)^{-1}$ and on the right by $\widetilde\gamma_{P^p,Q^q}^{-1}$ to obtain
$$(A^n)^{-1}w_{p,q}=v_{p,q}\widetilde\gamma_{P^p,Q^q}^{-1}.$$
This is the restriction of the inverse of the actual composite $A$, rather than a separately chosen inverse candidate. Hence $A^{-1}A=1$ and $AA^{-1}=1$. If $D_{\rm src},D_{\rm tgt}$ denote the differentials, $D_{\rm tgt}A=AD_{\rm src}$ gives $D_{\rm src}A^{-1}=A^{-1}D_{\rm tgt}$ by multiplying by the inverses in adjacent degrees. These are the signed differentials used in Step 1; additivity carries the coefficient $(-1)^p$ through each functor. Thus both inverse equations and the chain equation hold as chain maps.

source.place: Tag 0FPQ, lemma-symmetric-monoidal-cat-complexes, proof hints on the degree-zero unit and the induced constraints; agent calculation for the specified functor-square conjugation.

proof.text:
The description of $j$ in [lem-sfb-termwise-strong-monoidal], applied successively to the four functors, computes $J^0$ as
$$\epsilon^{E_1}E_1(\epsilon^{F_{\mathrm i}})a_{\mathbf1}^{-1}F_{\mathrm s}((\epsilon^{E_0})^{-1})=\widetilde\epsilon.$$
In other degrees every object involved is a zero object. Indeed an additive functor sends $0$ to a zero object since $1_{F0}=F(1_0)=F(0)=0$. There is a unique map between any two such objects. The composite $J$ has those components and is a chain isomorphism, since each of its factors is one. Its component formula is therefore exactly the asserted one.

source.place: Tag 0FPQ, lemma-symmetric-monoidal-cat-complexes, proof hints on the degree-zero unit and the induced constraints; agent calculation for the specified functor-square conjugation.

proof.text:
Abbreviate the total tensor by $B(P,Q)$. Put $G=F_{\mathrm s}E_0$ and $h=\gamma^{E_0}$. In $\widehat A=A F_{\mathrm s}(T_{E_0})$ and $\widehat J=J F_{\mathrm s}(j_{E_0})$, adjacent inverse comparisons cancel. Likewise
$$g_{M,N}=(a_M\otimes a_N)\gamma^{E_1}_{F_{\mathrm i}M,F_{\mathrm i}N}E_1(\gamma^{F_{\mathrm i}}_{M,N})a_{M\otimes N}^{-1},\quad e=\epsilon^{E_1}E_1(\epsilon^{F_{\mathrm i}})a_{\mathbf1}^{-1}.$$
Compose the forward summand equation of [lem-pd-total-oplax-conjugation-summands] with the summand equation for $T_{E_0}$ from [lem-sfb-termwise-strong-monoidal]. For every pair of complexes $X,Y$, with degreewise inclusion $i^{X,Y}_{s,t}$, this gives
$$\widehat A_{X,Y}G(i^{X,Y}_{s,t})=i^{GX,GY}_{s,t}g_{X^s,Y^t}.$$
The maps $g$ are natural: each factor in its displayed formula is natural, so for $u:M\to M',v:N\to N'$,
$$g_{M',N'}G(u\otimes v)=(Gu\otimes Gv)g_{M,N}.$$
Similarly $\widehat J^0=e$. No identification with the separate tensorator of $F_{\mathrm s}$ is used.

source.place: Tag 0FPQ, lemma-symmetric-monoidal-cat-complexes, proof hints on the degree-zero unit and the induced constraints; agent calculation for the specified functor-square conjugation.

proof.text:
Fix $p+q+r=n$, and put $M=P^p,N=Q^q,L=H^r$. Write $i_{p,q}=i^{P,Q}_{p,q}$ and $k_{q,r}=i^{Q,H}_{q,r}$. The source left-nested inclusion is
$$s=i^{B(P,Q),H}_{p+q,r}(i_{p,q}\otimes1).$$
The right-nested inclusion is $t=i^{P,B(Q,H)}_{p,q+r}(1\otimes k_{q,r})$. By [lem-sfb-total-tensor-homotopy], whose associator is induced by the ordinary associator and triple reindexing,
$$\alpha^{\rm Ch}s=t\alpha_{M,N,L}.$$
Use primed symbols for the same inclusions for $GP,GQ,GH$. Then $\alpha^{\rm Ch}s'=t'\alpha_{GM,GN,GL}$. For tensor products of chain maps their effect on inclusions is precisely the tensor of the indicated degree maps by [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso]. These formulas specify the inclusions and the intermediate reassociation maps used in the next two calculations; there is no permutation of degrees and hence no extra Koszul sign.

source.place: Tag 0FPQ, lemma-symmetric-monoidal-cat-complexes, proof hints on the degree-zero unit and the induced constraints; agent calculation for the specified functor-square conjugation.

proof.text:
For the first associator path, Step 5 first replaces $G(\alpha^{\rm Ch})G(s)$ by $G(t)G(\alpha_{M,N,L})$. The next intermediate map is computed using Step 4 and its naturality with the ordinary morphism $k_{q,r}:N\otimes L\to B(Q,H)^{q+r}$:
$$\widehat A_{P,B(Q,H)}G(t)=i^{GP,G B(Q,H)}_{p,q+r}(1\otimes G(k_{q,r}))g_{M,N\otimes L}.$$
Finally $1\otimes\widehat A_{Q,H}$ takes this outer inclusion to the corresponding inclusion followed by $1\otimes(\widehat A_{Q,H}^{q+r}G(k_{q,r}))$. Substitute Step 4 again to obtain exactly
$$t'(1\otimes g_{N,L})g_{M,N\otimes L}G(\alpha_{M,N,L}).$$
Thus both intermediate comparisons and the complete first path have their asserted ordinary restrictions, not just an equality after using coherence.

source.place: Tag 0FPQ, lemma-symmetric-monoidal-cat-complexes, proof hints on the degree-zero unit and the induced constraints; agent calculation for the specified functor-square conjugation.

proof.text:
For the second path, naturality in Step 4 with $i_{p,q}:M\otimes N\to B(P,Q)^{p+q}$ gives the first intermediate restriction
$$\widehat A_{B(P,Q),H}G(s)=i^{G B(P,Q),GH}_{p+q,r}(G(i_{p,q})\otimes1)g_{M\otimes N,L}.$$
Next $\widehat A_{P,Q}\otimes1$ changes this to $s'(g_{M,N}\otimes1)g_{M\otimes N,L}$ by the tensor-map formula and the summand equation of Step 4. The final target associator changes $s'$ to $t'\alpha_{GM,GN,GL}$ by Step 5. Therefore the complete restriction is
$$t'\alpha_{GM,GN,GL}(g_{M,N}\otimes1)g_{M\otimes N,L},$$
which is the specified ordinary second path. This records each intermediate map as well as the final composite.

source.place: Tag 0FPQ, lemma-symmetric-monoidal-cat-complexes, proof hints on the degree-zero unit and the induced constraints; agent calculation for the specified functor-square conjugation.

proof.text: Let $I=\mathbf1_{\mathcal A_0}[0]$ and, in this step, $M=P^n$. For the left unit, its only possibly nonzero source summand is $\mathbf1\otimes P^n$ in bidegree $(0,n)$. The induced unitor of [lem-sfb-total-tensor-homotopy] restricts there to $\lambda_M$, so the path $G(\lambda^{\rm Ch})$ restricts to $G(\lambda_M)$. The other path first has restriction $i^{GI,GP}_{0,n}g_{\mathbf1,M}$ by Step 4; then $\widehat J\otimes1$ replaces its first factor by $e$, and finally the target unitor gives $\lambda_{GM}(e\otimes1)g_{\mathbf1,M}$. For the right unit the corresponding summand is $(n,0)$, and the same three specified maps give $G(\rho_M)$ and $\rho_{GM}(1\otimes e)g_{M,\mathbf1}$, respectively. If the unit degree is nonzero its tensor factor is zero: tensoring preserves the empty coproduct by hypothesis, so its tensor with any object is zero. All restrictions on such summands are the unique zero maps. The tensor-map rule is [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso], and the components of $\widehat J$ were computed in Steps 3-4.

source.place: Tag 0FPQ, lemma-symmetric-monoidal-cat-complexes, proof hints on the degree-zero unit and the induced constraints; agent calculation for the specified functor-square conjugation.

proof.text: To check that these are the specified transported diagrams, expand $\widehat A=(a\otimes a)T_{E_1}E_1(T_{F_{\mathrm i}})a^{-1}_{B(-,-)}$ from Step 4. At each inner total $B(Q,H)$ or $B(P,Q)$, the $a$ from the outer comparison cancels the $a^{-1}$ from the inner comparison. Move the outer $a^{-1}$ past the source associator by its naturality. The remaining $E_1$ comparisons are precisely its associator comparisons from [lem-sfb-termwise-strong-monoidal], so the two expanded paths are the images of the two internal paths with the indicated source and target comparisons. The same cancellation at $I$ uses $\widehat J=j_{E_1}E_1(j_{F_{\mathrm i}})a_I^{-1}$ and the two unit identities of that lemma. These operations use naturality of $a$ and inverse cancellation, with no monoidal equation for $a$. Reinsert $A=\widehat A F_{\mathrm s}(T_{E_0}^{-1})$ and $J=\widehat J F_{\mathrm s}(j_{E_0}^{-1})$ at each occurrence. On an ordinary summand these added maps are exactly $F_{\mathrm s}(h^{-1})$ and $F_{\mathrm s}((\epsilon^{E_0})^{-1})$, respectively, by the summand and degree-zero formulas of that lemma. Hence Steps 6-8 give the original $A,J$ paths including each added comparison, with $\widetilde\gamma=gF_{\mathrm s}(h^{-1})$ and $\widetilde\epsilon=eF_{\mathrm s}((\epsilon^{E_0})^{-1})$.

source.place: Tag 0FPQ, lemma-symmetric-monoidal-cat-complexes, proof hints on the degree-zero unit and the induced constraints; agent calculation for the specified functor-square conjugation.

proof.text: Finally the restrictions determine maps on the whole totals. For two maps from a coproduct, equality after every injection implies equality by uniqueness in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]; the preserved cocones supplied by [lem-pd-total-oplax-conjugation-summands] give the same test after applying $F_{\mathrm s}$ or $G$. For a nested triple sum first fix its outer degree and apply that uniqueness to the inner sum after tensoring with the remaining object (tensoring preserves this coproduct by hypothesis), then apply uniqueness to the outer sum. After $E_0$, the inner family is a preserved double-tensor coproduct cocone tensored with $E_0H^r$: use the natural strong tensorator to identify this with $E_0$ of the inner tensored cocone. Hence it is again a coproduct, by the summand lemma and the tensor-preservation hypothesis. The outer cocone is a degreewise tensor-total cocone, also preserved by that lemma. Finally $F_{\mathrm s}$ preserves both countable cocones by hypothesis. Thus equality on every nested triple inclusion implies equality in every degree. For units the same test applies to the double sum. Equality in every degree is equality of chain maps. The ordinary path equalities, whenever imposed, therefore imply the total path equalities. This proof neither truncates an infinite sum nor needs flatness or boundedness.
